setup: The differential \(dy = f'(x)\,dx\) estimates the change in \(y = x^{2}\) from \(x = [[x0]]\) when \(x\) moves by \(dx = [[dx]]\).

steps.say: Differentiate: \(f'(x) = 2x\), so at \(x = [[x0]]\) the slope is \(f'([[x0]]) = [[fpx]]\).
Multiply the slope by the step: \(dy = [[fpx]] \cdot [[dx]] = [[dy]]\).
For comparison, the exact change is \(\Delta y = ([[x1]])^{2} - [[x0]]^{2} = [[fx1]] - [[fx0]] = [[exact]]\): the differential is the linear estimate, close but not equal.
